task 2: signed-in requests carry the bearer token
task 3: protected pages redirect to login and return after sign-in
task 4: admin screens and controls follow the signed-in role
task 5: a 401 clears the session and returns to login with an explanation
task 6: a 403 shows a not-allowed message without signing the user out

cleanup.notes: Setup (npm ci in tests/) creates tests/node_modules; the optional dev setup (npm ci in starter/) creates starter/node_modules. Cleanup deletes both; the tests create nothing else. The tests stub fetch and never use the network; the dev server's mock API is local. The mock accounts, passwords and tokens (avery/beacon1, omar/beacon2, tok-avery, tok-omar) are fake development fixtures, not secrets. The session is kept in React state only; nothing is written to browser storage. Resetting the learner's work means restoring starter/src from a fresh copy of the lab. The expected output file writes variable timings as <ms>, and test file lines may print in any order. The 25-minute median and 30-minute cap are planning figures for the module's S34 guided lab slot, not a measured learner pilot. Setup (the one-time npm ci) completes before the lab slot's working time; the 30-minute allowance covers only work on the tasks. The javascript-fundamentals-review objectives and react-review#o1 are exercised as scored production work across the tasks (destructuring, spread, map/filter, async/await tracing and ES modules appear throughout); react-review#o2 (bug-class diagnosis) is deliberately not claimed by this lab; the react-review topic page practises it. Partial-objective note: turning-off-the-dev-profile#o2 is scored here only for its Vite-environment-variable clause (plus the front-end auto-sign-in twin); the Spring-profile clause is practised on the topic page, not in this lab. All assertions are behavioral through Testing Library against rendered output and the recorded fetch calls; no test reads the learner's source text.
